source.title: NeuroInspect: Interpretable Neuron-based Debugging Framework through Class-conditional Visualizations
source.authors: Yeong-Joon Ju; Ji-Hoon Park; Seong-Whan Lee

record.tranche_reason: The study examines whether vision-model neurons represent multiple concepts using feature visualizations and class-conditioned visualizations, a different measurement from the original examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports examples of neurons visualized as representing multiple concepts. Human preference scores compare visualization methods, not polysemanticity, so they are not rows. Results about editing decision layers and classifier accuracy do not measure the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper's main contribution is a debugging framework, but Section III-D and IV-A (Figs. 2–3) report a direct observation bearing on V1. Penultimate-layer neurons of an ImageNet ResNet-18 respond to several semantically distant inputs: water jets, lattice bridges, dog and monkey faces, and holed objects. This is a new architecture (ResNet rather than InceptionV1), studied qualitatively.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that neurons can hold abstract, mixed, multifaceted features that plain FV renders as convoluted images. Class-conditional CLIP-Illusion isolates these into class-specific, human-interpretable views. The framework's main claims concern debugging and mitigating spurious correlations.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation-maximizing and CLIP-constrained class-conditioned visualizations rather than the original source's neuron examples and analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The visual interpretation differs between ordinary feature visualization and class-conditioned CLIP-Illusion; the paper also reports that class-specific features become more pronounced as gamma increases.
record.problems: The relevant evidence is qualitative and based on a few illustrated neurons; the study does not estimate the share of polysemantic neurons or validate whether the depicted concepts are independent jobs.
record.rows_left_out: Human preference results in Table I compare interpretability of visualization methods rather than measuring neuron polysemanticity. Editing and classification-performance results in Tables II–IV do not measure the claim.

untested.parts: InceptionV1 and its canonical neurons; how common polysemantic neurons are across the layer; layers other than the penultimate one.
Causes of polysemanticity, including superposition and capacity, are not examined.
Initialization, regularization or noise as causes are not examined.
No comparison across architectures, activation functions or regularization.
The paper does not test whether mixed-looking neurons detect one shared feature. CLIP-Illusion separates facets but never evaluates whether they are unified.
Visualization method and gamma are varied, but neurons are never scored as polysemantic or not under different criteria.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence for polysemanticity is incidental motivation for the visualization method. It rests on a few hand-picked neurons, with no quantification and no controls. I removed the reader's V6 'challenges' verdict because the study never examines whether the facets share one feature. Appendix Fig. 9 notes that at low gamma, visualizations conditioned on different classes look similar. This is weak and unexamined, so it is not a test of V6. Table I (human preference) and Tables II–IV (editing and accuracy) evaluate the authors' own method and are correctly left out as rows.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies ResNet neurons, not InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55, and does not quantify how common the behavior is across neurons.
Language models and transformer MLP neurons.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Comparisons of polysemanticity across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, including SoLU.
The study does not test whether the specific InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 has a shared feature, or establish how often mixed-looking neurons have a unified job.
The study varies visualization methods and settings but does not score or measure whether neurons count as polysemantic under different activation ranges or explanation criteria.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, neuron 3 of the penultimate layer
rows.operation_detail: Feature visualization by activation maximization from Gaussian noise
rows.measure: Visualized features associated with the neuron
rows.value: The paper describes the images as abstract and mixed with several characteristics of the neuron.
rows.note: The text says the FV images are difficult to interpret and show multiple characteristics; this is a qualitative visualization result, not a rate across neurons.
rows.check: Link is acceptable. The evidence is FV images described as mixed, plus top-activated images from unrelated classes (garden spider, scuba diver, ballpoint pen, ice lolly). It covers one hand-picked neuron and gives no rate.

source_check.problem: Accurate. This is a qualitative remark that FV images for neuron 3 are 'abstract and mixed with several characteristics' (citing [14]), with no rate across neurons.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, neuron 0 of the penultimate layer
rows.measure: Concepts associated with the neuron in its most activating images
rows.value: The paper states that the images indicate multiple concepts with distant semantics; examples include fireboat and fountain, bridge types, dog breeds and primates, and objects with holes.
rows.note: Qualitative examples are presented for one neuron; the study does not establish how frequently this occurs.
rows.check: Remove the V6 link. The authors never ask whether these concepts share a single underlying feature. Calling them 'distant semantics' is a description, not a test showing that a unifying reading fails.

source_check.problem: Accurate. The text asserts this for neuron 0. The Fig. 3 captions list water jet, lattice boom/open spandrel, dog face, monkey-like face and iron with holes.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, neuron 0 of the penultimate layer

conditions.value: 25 classes most related to the neuron based on decision-layer coefficients

rows.measure: Concepts represented in visualizations conditioned on classes
rows.value: The paper identifies long diagonal lines, multiple round holes, and animal faces as concepts represented by the neuron.
rows.note: The authors present the class-conditioned images as views of multiple facets of the same neuron.
rows.check: Link is acceptable. The concepts were picked by the authors to match top-activated images, conditioned on the 25 classes with the highest decision-layer coefficients. The result is illustrative, not systematic.

labels.reason: V1 is an existence claim. Neuron 0's top-activated images span distant concepts (r2), its class-conditioned views separate them into lines, holes and faces (r3), and neuron 3's FV is mixed (r1). The effect appears as V1 describes in this setting.

relation.reason: The study's own visualizations bear, qualitatively, on whether some image-classifier neurons respond to unrelated inputs. The test is weak (two hand-picked neurons, no prevalence, no controls), but it is a test of V1.

tranche.reason: Fig. 3 and Section IV-A report the study's own observation: ResNet-18 neuron 0's top-activated images show several concepts with distant semantics. This is a result in a new setting (ResNet-18, not InceptionV1) that bears on V1's existence claim. The paper does not report only its own method's performance, so T4 does not apply.

source_check.notes: The evidence is two hand-picked neurons, shown qualitatively, in a debugging-method paper, with no prevalence and no controls. Neuron 0's CLIP-Illusion panels were chosen to match its top-image concepts. In Fig. 2, the class names (garden spider, scuba diver, ballpoint pen, ice lolly and so on) label the CLIP-Illusion panels, not the top-activated images. The text says neuron 3's top images do not show the spider concept.

statements.correction: Neuron 0 (ResNet-18 penultimate layer, pre-trained on ImageNet): the top-activated real images show a water jet, a lattice boom/open spandrel, a dog face, a monkey-like face and iron with holes. The class-conditioned CLIP-Illusion views (25 classes ranked by beta) are labelled long diagonal lines, multiple round holes and animal faces. The text describes neuron 3's FV images as abstract and mixed.
statements.problem: Correct for this study. The units are hand-picked, the evidence is qualitative, and it is a method paper. It is correctly described as a preprint with code and no controls.
